definitions: To turn from one side to the other, or from the back to the front, or vice versa.
To transfer or carry forward an amount or balance from one period to the next.
To defer or postpone something, especially a debt or loan.
To yield or submit to someone or something, often under pressure.
examples: The dog loves to roll over for belly rubs.
We decided to roll over the remaining budget to next quarter.
The bank allowed them to roll over their loan for another month.
The company had to roll over to the demands of the striking workers.
